proposed_core_edits.proposed: \(D_k(n)=\max_{(G,T,e)\in\mathcal G_{n,k},\ d_e(G)<\infty}[K_G(\lambda_e):K_G]\). For \(n\geq4\), the proved two-sided envelope is \(2^{\min\{k+1,\lfloor(n-2)/2\rfloor\}}\leq D_k(n)\leq\vartheta_{n-1,k+1}\leq\min\{2^{k+1},\tau_{n-1}\}\). The exact maximality characterizations are \(\vartheta_{N,g}=2^g\) if and only if \(N\geq2g+1\), and, for every admissible \((n,k)\), \(D_k(n)=2^{k+1}\) if and only if \(n\geq2k+4\); in particular, \(D_k(n)<2^{k+1}\) below that size threshold. The exact five-vertex orientation recurrence is \((\vartheta_{5,g})_{g=0}^{6}=(1,2,4,6,8,12,24)\), giving \(D_2(6)\leq6\), \(D_3(6)\leq8\), \(D_4(6)\leq12\), and \(D_k(6)\leq24\) for admissible \(k\geq5\); the established equalities are \(D_0(6)=2\) and \(D_1(6)=4\). The exact table is \(D_0(2)=1\), \(D_k(3)=1\), \(D_k(4)=2\), \(D_0(5)=2\), \(D_1(5)=3\), and \(D_k(5)=4\) for \(k\geq2\). At zero excess the dispatcher returns the exact published \(1/2/\infty\) tree classification and finite \(\operatorname{FASTP}\) expressions; at positive excess its unconditional algebraic branch retains the explicit computable report \(d_e(G)\leq2^{\min\{|D|-n+2,\binom{n-2}{2}\}}\) and does not claim to compute \(\vartheta_{n-1,k+1}\). A rational-circuit representation of \(p_e(t)\) is delivered only under the valid-chart and successful-output conditions of \(\mathrm{thm:conditional\mbox{-}geometric\mbox{-}resolution}\).

prose_updates.tldr: Adding parents to a supplied rooted tree creates finite ambiguity measured here by the single-coordinate complex degree \(D_k(n)\), not by whole-fiber cardinality or real root count. For \(n\geq4\), the paper proves \(2^{\min\{k+1,\lfloor(n-2)/2\rfloor\}}\leq D_k(n)\leq\vartheta_{n-1,k+1}\leq\min\{2^{k+1},\tau_{n-1}\}\), where \(\vartheta_{N,g}\) maximizes prescribed-indegree orientation fibers jointly over at most \(N\) vertices and cycle rank at most \(g\). The exact combinatorial maximality threshold is \(\vartheta_{N,g}=2^g\) if and only if \(N\geq2g+1\); combined with the one-sink construction and the orientation upper bound, this gives the exact SEM threshold \(D_k(n)=2^{k+1}\) if and only if \(n\geq2k+4\). Thus the frontier is strictly below \(2^{k+1}\) below that threshold, although its exact values remain open in the positive-excess, at-least-six-vertex strip. The exact five-vertex orientation recurrence \((1,2,4,6,8,12,24)\) yields the six-vertex caps \(6,8,12,24\), but \(\vartheta\) is not claimed SEM-attained in the unresolved strip. The zero-excess dispatcher retains the complete published \(1/2/\infty\) classification and finite expressions; positive excess retains the existing efficiently reportable size-binomial cap, while exact polynomials, exceptional sets, real lifting, and regular inference remain chart-conditional.

project_justification.fill: The paper proves the coupled projection-aware envelope \(2^{\min\{k+1,\lfloor(n-2)/2\rfloor\}}\leq D_k(n)\leq\vartheta_{n-1,k+1}\leq\min\{2^{k+1},\tau_{n-1}\}\) for \(n\geq4\). It proves the exact orientation maximality criterion \(\vartheta_{N,g}=2^g\) if and only if \(N\geq2g+1\), and, with the one-sink attaining family, the headline criterion \(D_k(n)=2^{k+1}\) if and only if \(n\geq2k+4\). It also gives the checkable recurrence \((\vartheta_{5,g})_{g=0}^{6}=(1,2,4,6,8,12,24)\), the resulting six-vertex row, the inherited all-size lower envelope, and the exact \(n\leq5\) coordinate-degree frontier. In the remaining positive-excess, \(n\geq6\) strip below the threshold, strict submaximality is proved but the exact frontier is left open; the combinatorial ceiling is not claimed SEM-attained there. The paper supplies an unconditional randomized Jacobian-rank tag, retains the complete published tree-case output at \(k=0\), and proves a conditional geometric-resolution theorem with explicit straight-line-program and intermediate-degree dependence. Exceptional-set, real-lifting, and regular-inference results hold only on the supplied-valid-chart and successful-output domain.

prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: For \(k>0\), \(n\geq6\), and \(n<2k+4\), one now has the strict submaximality \(D_k(n)<2^{k+1}\), but the exact frontier remains between \(2^{\min\{k+1,\lfloor(n-2)/2\rfloor\}}\) and \(\vartheta_{n-1,k+1}\). The latter is only a combinatorial upper bound: SEM branches may be lost through forced covariance relations, exact localization, affine dehomogenization, or projective infinity. The six-vertex recurrence sharpens this upper bound to \(6,8,12,24\) for \(k=2,3,4,\geq5\), respectively, but no attaining SEM family is asserted. The unconditional fixed-parameter dispatcher retains the efficiently explicit size-binomial cap because this round supplies no uniform exact computation and certificate for \(\vartheta_{n-1,k+1}\) within its runtime. The exhaustive five-node orbit census remains a secondary regression and coordinate-census question because the cubic and quartic base cases and the entire \(n\leq5\) frontier are fixed. Independently, the quadratic core does not construct a reduced local presentation of the embedded source prime or bounded rational-circuit descent over \(K_G\). On the certified event determined by a supplied valid source-prime chart, the exceptional-set theorem, real-root-lifting theorem, regular-cell lemma, derived root-separation lemma, regular finite-set inference theorem, and singleton inference proposition hold. Their chart antecedent appears in every statement; no chart-free statistical theorem is asserted. Coordinate localization is never promoted to equality of full fibers, real roots are never equated with real supported lifts, and local rank is not used to assert real uniqueness.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The paper proves the full frontier through five vertices, the all-size lower envelope, and the coupled upper bound \(D_k(n)\leq\vartheta_{n-1,k+1}\leq\min\{2^{k+1},\tau_{n-1}\}\). It proves \(\vartheta_{N,g}=2^g\) if and only if \(N\geq2g+1\), and \(D_k(n)=2^{k+1}\) if and only if \(n\geq2k+4\); below the latter threshold the frontier is strictly submaximal, but its exact values remain open for positive excess and at least six vertices. The recurrence \((\vartheta_{5,g})_{g=0}^{6}=(1,2,4,6,8,12,24)\) yields \(D_2(6)\leq6\), \(D_3(6)\leq8\), \(D_4(6)\leq12\), and \(D_k(6)\leq24\) for admissible \(k\geq5\), alongside the established \(D_0(6)=2\) and \(D_1(6)=4\). The joint orientation quantity remains only an upper bound and is not claimed SEM-attained in the unresolved strip. Unconditionally, the dispatcher returns the complete published \(1/2/\infty\) classification and finite \(\operatorname{FASTP}\) expressions on \(\mathcal G_{n,0}\). For \(|D\setminus T|>0\), it returns only a randomized algebraic-versus-transcendental tag, a rank or dominance certificate, and the efficiently available ceiling \(d_e(G)\leq2^{\min\{|D|-n+2,\binom{n-2}{2}\}}\); it does not compute \(\vartheta_{n-1,k+1}\), \(d_e(G)\), \(p_e\), \(\mathcal Q_{G,e}\), or \(h_{G,e}\) on the algebraic branch. Given valid source-prime charts and successful output, the conditional geometric-resolution theorem returns the exact finite objects with its stated straight-line-program and intermediate-degree dependence. On precisely that same conditional domain, the exceptional-set, real-lifting, and regular-inference results hold. No discriminant-uniform inference, automatic branch selection, or all-singular-covariance guarantee is claimed, and positive definiteness of recovered noise follows only after a complete real supported lift by congruence.
